sentences.text:
Satendra Kumar Jain And 2 Others vs State Of Up And 5 Others
on 12 December, 2024

Author: Mahesh Chandra Tripathi
Bench: Mahesh Chandra Tripathi
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:194951-Db
Court No. - 42
Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 148 of 2024
Petitioner :- Satendra Kumar Jain and 2 others
Respondent :- State of Up and 5 others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Ranvijay Chaubey

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Yash Padia Hon'ble Mahesh Chandra Tripathi,J.
Hon'ble Prashant Kumar,J.
1. Heard Sri Manoj Kumar Singh, Advocate, holding brief of Sri Ranvijay Chaubey, learned counsel for the petitioners; Sri Shashidhar Pandey, learned A.G.A, for the State respondents and Sri Yash Padia, learned counsel for the respondent no.3.
2.

The relief sought in this petition is for quashing of the impugned FIR dated 01.11.2023 registered as Case Crime No.470 of 2023 under Sections 409, 417, 419, 420, 422, 465, 467, 468, 471, 506, 120B IPC, Police Station Bilari, District Moradabad.
Further prayer has been made not to arrest the petitioners in the aforesaid case.

sentences.text: The matter was taken up on 8.2.2024 and considering the commercial dispute, the Division Bench had referred the matter to the Mediation Centre of this Court.

For ready reference, the same is reproduced herein below:-
"1. The petitioners, by means of this writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, are before this Court with a prayer to quash the impugned First Information Report dated 1.11.2023 registered as Case Crime No. 470 of 2023, under Sections 409, 417, 419, 420, 422, 465, 467, 468, 471, 506, 120-B IPC, Police Station- Bilari, District- Moradabad.

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners; Sri Tarun Agrawal and Sri Yash Padia,
learned counsel for the respondent no. 3 and the learned A.G.A. for the State-respondent.
3.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners that the present matter relates to commercial transaction, which may be amicably settled by way of mediation and conciliation, therefore, the matter may be referred to the Mediation and Conciliation Centre of this Court.

4. In view of the above, it is directed that petitioners shall deposit a sum of Rs. One Crore by way of demand draft in favour of sixth respondent within three weeks from today and further demand draft of Rs. 10,000/- made in favour of 'Allahabad High Court Mediation and Conciliation Centre' shall be deposited with the Mediation Centre and the same may be retained by the Mediation Centre as mediation fee.
5.

The matter is remitted to the Mediation Centre with the direction that after deposit of such amount by the petitioners, it shall issue notice to the parties fixing some date for mediation and shall make all possible efforts to conclude the mediation and conciliation proceedings expeditiously, preferably within a period of six weeks.

6. List this matter again on 18.4.2024 before the appropriate Bench along with the report of Mediation Centre.
7.
Till the next date of listing, respondents are restrained to arrest the petitioners pursuant to the impugned F.I.R. subject to cooperation in the on-going investigation.

8. It is made clear that in case there occurs default by the petitioners either in depositing the amount or in appearing before the Mediation Centre on the date fixed,
the interim order shall cease to operate and the Mediation Centre shall immediately communicate with the office which in turn shall list the case within a week before the appropriate Bench for passing orders in the matter."
4.

Sri Yash Padia, learned counsel for the informant has vehemently opposed the writ petition and submits that on one hand, on the request of the petitioners' counsel, on the instructions on behalf of Satendra Kumar Jain And 2 Others vs State Of Up And 5 Others on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64202981/
2 the petitioners, the matter was referred to the Mediation Centre and on the other hand, instead of depositing the amount in question, the petitioners had approached to the Apex Court by preferring Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No.2704 of 2024 (Satendra Kumar Jain & ors vs. the State of Uttar Pradesh) and Hon'ble Apex Court vide order dated 02.09.2024 has dismissed the same with detailed observations.

sentences.text:
For ready reference, the order is reproduced herein under:-
"This matter is pending before the High Court.
The High Court vide the impugned order dated 08.02.2024 directed the petitioner to deposit Rupees One Crore as a condition prior to sending the matter for mediation.
The petitioner admits a debt of Rs.90 lacs though the demand is of Rs.2.62 crores.
Under these circumstances, we see absolutely nothing wrong by the High Court directing the petitioner to deposit an amount of Rupees One Crore.
There is no occasion for us to interfere, particularly at this stage.
The special leave petition is dismissed.
Pending application (s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

Interim order shall stand vacated."
5.
We have occasion to peruse the record in question and find that the petitioners had obtained the interim order on 08.02.2024 and the matter had also been dragged before the Mediation Centre.

Various dates i.e. 16.04.2024, 30.04.2024, 14.05.2024, 28.05.2024, 09.07.2024, 23.07.2024,
13.08.2024, 27.08.2024, 10.09.2024 and 24.09.2024 were fixed but on account of non-cooperation of the petitioners, the same could not be finalized and eventually, the mediation has failed.
The impugned FIR discloses cognizable offence.

Even at the admission stage, the petitioners had prayed for referring the matter to the mediation centre but instead of best endeavour of the Court, the parties could not resolve the controversy and the order dated 08.02.2024 is already approved by the Apex Court on 02.09.2024.

In view of the law laid down by Hon?ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana and others vs. Bhajan Lal and others, 1992 Supp. (1) SCC 335 and M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra, AIR 2021 SC 1918 and in Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No.3262/2021 (Leelavati Devi @ Leelawati & another vs. the State of Uttar Pradesh) decided on 07.10.2021, no case has been made out for interference with the impugned first information report.

7. It is made clear that we have not adjudicated the contentions raised by learned counsel for the petitioners and the same are left open for the petitioners to raise at an appropriate stage in an appropriate proceeding, in accordance with law.
